# Lab 0d · Modeling using budgets {background-color="#1a3a5c"}


# 3 · What is uncertainty? {background-color="#1a3a5c"}

## Three reasons a forecast model can be wrong {.smaller}

> "It's tough to make predictions, especially about the future."

You just generated all three in the bucket:

- **Initial-condition uncertainty** — you varied $h_0$: matters early, forgotten later *(Earth: today's exact weather)*
- **Model uncertainty** — you varied $k$: parameters (and structure) *(Earth: we don't know exact laws or our models can't be exactly solved)*
- **Scenario uncertainty** — you varied $F$: the pourer decides, not physics *(Earth: emissions)*

Different ones dominate at different horizons. 

::: {.notes}
Every bullet points at something they DID today. Worth saying aloud: by 2100 the biggest uncertainty is the scenario — the largest unknown is a choice.
:::

## How the three trade off with time {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/ipcc_ar6_faq4_1_temp.png){height="320px" fig-align="center"}
<div style="font-size:0.8em; line-height:1.2;">Individual model runs under a low and a high scenario. For the next ~20 years the wiggles — <b>internal variability</b> — swamp the difference between scenarios.</div>
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/hawkins_fracvar_global_T.png){height="320px" fig-align="center"}
<div style="font-size:0.8em; line-height:1.2;">Share of the uncertainty in <b>global, annual-mean, 10-year-averaged</b> temperature: <span style="color:#f28c00"><b>internal variability</b></span> dominates early, <span style="color:#1f1fff"><b>model uncertainty</b></span> mid-century, <span style="color:#0a7a0a"><b>scenario</b></span> by 2100. <em>That smoothing is why orange fades so fast — ask about one summer in one city and it stays orange much longer.</em></div>
:::
::::

<div style="font-size:0.35em; color:#888;">Left: IPCC AR6 WG1 FAQ 4.1 (2021). Right: Hawkins &amp; Sutton (2009), updated for CMIP5 by E. Hawkins, Climate Lab Book, CC BY-SA 4.0.</div>

::: {.notes}
Map the bucket onto the colours: varying h0 = orange, varying k = blue, varying F = green. Left panel is the intuition (you cannot tell the scenarios apart before ~2040); right panel is the bookkeeping. Closing line: by 2100 the biggest uncertainty is the scenario — the largest unknown is a choice.
:::
